status: closed, honest partial: complete for the dispatched scope with three rows named unrun
missionPremise: The operator hand-off brief said the PDF export path could be replaced OR configured. The planner measured the live SmartCity bundle and ruled that replace is the only option, on the reasoning that html2canvas rasterises the DOM and jsPDF wraps the bitmap, so the output fails 504.2.2 and also 1.1.1 and 1.4.5. G-96 exists to test that reasoning across the product line rather than inherit it, and to recommend what replaces it. The dispatch explicitly stated that reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome, per DEV_PROCESS 3.2. It was, and the verdict survived while the rationale did not.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this lane as done when five things are true. One: every document-emitting path across smartcity-dashboards, smart-files, plan-review and the original SmartCity is listed with its generator, its client-or-server placement, its library, and a measured verdict on text layer, /StructTreeRoot, /MarkInfo, /Lang and title, with the measuring command named per cell. Two: the surface that produced 48021_34649_site_plan.pdf is established by an evidence chain rather than asserted. Three: a generator is recommended with its trade-off and with its cost priced against the actual shape of these repos, which have no build step and one dependency. Four: the number of document types is stated with its counting rule, split into what is one fix and what is many. Five: each of the five 504.2.2 properties has a named verification method that has already been demonstrated on a real file, and anything not determined is named as unrun with the reason and with what would be run.
scopeBasis: In scope: the four surfaces the dispatch named, plus hauska-engine and hauska-map, which the site-plan question forces in because the artifact could not otherwise be traced. Out of scope with basis rather than by omission: legacy-design-tools' second pdf-lib family, because the Plan Review that the Dashboards shell actually mounts was established by live GET to be the new plan-review repo and no dispatched surface serves the LDT family; atx-bulls' pdf-lib waiver renderer, because it is not in the sellable govtech line; and the smartcity-os repository source, because the served bundle is the customer-facing artifact and was measured directly. Running any generator was excluded by the dispatch, which is why two document types are code-measured and one surface is bundle-measured rather than artifact-measured; each is named as unrun rather than presented as measured.

findings.finding: The SmartCity PDF export is NOT a raster. All application PDF paths draw vector text via jsPDF .text() and jspdf-autotable. html2canvas is bundled as an optional dependency of the jsPDF html() plugin and has zero call sites.
findings.evidence: `.html(` 0 and `API.html` 0 occurrences in 5,578,225 bytes; all 6 `addImage(` sites are library-internal; the shared helpers Pu, Ur, Kh, wf, Fm all emit text or autoTable.
findings.consequence: 1.1.1 and 1.4.5 must be dropped from the PDF rationale. A reviewer who opens one of these files will find selectable text.

findings.severity: confirms the verdict on new grounds
findings.finding: 504.2.2 still fails and replacement is still correct, because jsPDF 4.2.1 has no tagged-PDF capability at all.
findings.evidence: 0 occurrences of /StructTreeRoot and /MarkInfo in the bundle; jsPDF putCatalog writes only /Type /Catalog, /Pages, /OpenAction, /PageLayout and optional /PageMode. setLanguage and setDocumentProperties are defined once each and never called, so no /Lang and no title either.

findings.finding: smartcity-dashboards, smart-files and plan-review emit no documents at all, measured on the served bundles.
findings.evidence: Dashboards /app.js 44,233 bytes, Smart Files 24,929, Plan Review 33,987; zero hits for jsPDF, html2canvas, pdf-lib, window.print, application/pdf, text/csv and download. Dashboards' own Homes-table row 71 already carries disposition 'Not built'.

findings.finding: The site-plan PDF is produced by hauska-engine packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/pdf/render.ts with pdf-lib plus @pdf-lib/fontkit, served by engine-api at /:parcelNodeId/site-plan-export, and surfaced by SmartSite / Property Explorer in hauska-map.
findings.evidence: Four independent links: filenameFor in SitePlanExportSection.tsx produces exactly 48021_34649_site_plan.pdf; the HONESTY_LINE string matches the extracted page-1 text verbatim; render.ts:1152 builds the SP-48021-34649 sheet id; the served SmartSite bundle contains pe-site-plan-export and _site_plan.pdf and zero client PDF libraries.

findings.finding: The site-plan PDF's reading order is destroyed at the source. Tracked runs are drawn glyph by glyph, so 64.4 percent of extracted lines are a single character.
findings.evidence: render.ts:373 comment 'tracked runs are drawn glyph-by-glyph with an em-based advance'; measured 268 single-character lines of 416 total, counting rule stated. Page shares 57.8, 63.2, 69.1 percent.
findings.consequence: Adding tags to this renderer would produce a file that passes an automated tag check and still reads one letter at a time. The reading-order fix is a renderer change.

findings.finding: Dashboards generates no documents but a Dashboards user can still obtain an untagged pdf-lib PDF, because the shell mounts SmartSite as an iframe at smartsite.cloud and SmartSite carries the site-plan export.
findings.evidence: src/mounts.mjs smartsite origin https://smartsite.cloud with parcelPath /?parcelNodeId=.

findings.finding: Headless Chromium print-to-PDF already produces the full 504.2.2 property set in house, with no special effort.
findings.evidence: Four PDFs in P:/tmp produced 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14 by Skia/PDF m151 via HeadlessChrome/151, each carrying /MarkInfo Marked true, /StructTreeRoot, /Lang en, a real /Title and /ViewerPreferences DisplayDocTitle true. Structure walk of one: /Document 1, /H1 1, /H2 3, /P 4, /NonStruct 50.
findings.statedLimit: The /NonStruct 50 is the limit. Chromium tags what the HTML says, so tag quality is a direct function of HTML semantics.

findings.severity: minor, kept so it is not rediscovered as an accessibility defect
findings.finding: The SmartCity report-detail modal's Export PDF, Export Excel and Print buttons are simulated. They fire a toast, wait 1500ms on setTimeout, and fire 'Export Complete'. Nothing is produced.

recommendation.generator: Headless Chromium print-to-PDF from semantic HTML, run server-side, via ONE shared render service rather than a dependency in each product repo.
recommendation.tradeOff: Tag quality is inherited from HTML semantics, so this is not a swap that fixes conformance by itself; it makes the G-94 and G-95 semantic work count twice. Alternatives were tested and rejected: jsPDF has no structure-tree API so /StructTreeRoot is unreachable, and pdf-lib offers setTitle and setLanguage but no structure tree, which would buy two of five properties while the glyph-by-glyph renderer keeps failing reading order.
recommendation.costToTheseRepos: All three declare pg as their only dependency, run node src/server.mjs with no build step, and ship FROM node:22-alpine. Adding Puppeteer or Playwright means leaving alpine or apk add chromium, roughly 300 to 400 MB of image, a Cloud Run sandbox decision, and a cold start that includes a browser launch. The shared-service form keeps all three at one dependency and one fetch.
recommendation.cheapestAlternativeThatIsStillValid: Client-side window.print() against a print stylesheet. Zero new dependencies and the same Chromium code path, but the user gets a print dialog, filename control is limited, and tagging depends on the viewer's browser so an ACR cannot claim it uniformly. There are currently zero @media print rules across sc-kit.css, shell.css and styles.css in all three repos.
recommendation.smartSiteIsDifferent: Do not replace the site-plan renderer. Sequence: add setTitle and setLanguage to render.ts, dossier.ts and flood-drainage.ts, which removes two of five failures in three lines; then fix the tracked glyph-by-glyph runs, which is the reading-order fix and the one that matters; then decide whether the summary sheet is re-emitted as an HTML-derived tagged page.
